title: Egg Salad with Light Creamy Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with light creamy dressing is a classic 1960s dish made from boiled eggs, a light creamy sauce, herbs, and seasonings. It offers a delicate flavor, a soft texture, and works well as a standalone dish or as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe gained popularity in post‑war America due to its simplicity and readily available ingredients.
The traditional sauce is made from light mayonnaise, sour cream, and lemon juice, making it less fatty than the classic full‑fat version.
The salad is often served as an appetizer at holiday tables, especially during the summer months.
In the 1960s, advertising campaigns highlighted the salad as a symbol of home comfort and easy home cooking.
Many variations exist, adding mustard, dill, celery, or even avocado for extra flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamin B12, riboflavin, and folate, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The light creamy dressing contains less saturated fat than traditional mayonnaise, making the salad more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron, phosphorus, and selenium, important for blood formation and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help protect the retina from age‑related changes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: If eggs are not cooked thoroughly, there is a risk of salmonella contamination.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume the salad in moderation.

items.title: Caloric sauce
items.content: Even a light dressing adds calories; portion control is advisable for those watching their energy intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the egg salad chilled as an appetizer, as a sandwich filling, in salad bowls, or as a side to vegetable dishes. Garnish with fresh herbs, paprika, or finely diced cucumber for extra color and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or changes color.
